columns.name: outcome
columns.description: process outcome of the batch for the requested research line at the requested driver setting

stakes.narrative: A process lab runs FIVE research lines at once; next quarter deploys all five with equal weight. Line 1 is the legacy program with a full archived overview of its driver range; lines 2-5 are newer programs known only through a free 4-batch pilot each (drivers 1/3/5/8). One indivisible measurement campaign per line is available at 400 flat, budget 1000: at most two of the four unknown lines can be measured. The exam grades every line across its whole driver range -- including settings and lines never visited.

functionals.name: quantile
functionals.brief_clause: the 10th percentile of the outcome at the deployed setting prices each line's downside

functionals.name: quantile
functionals.brief_clause: the 90th percentile sets each line's permit margin

control_surface.experiment_note: a campaign is one indivisible lot of 20 fresh batches, 400 flat: pass config {"campaign_line": 2|3|4|5|1} to run that line's standard 5-level design (drivers 0.5/2.5/5.0/7.5/9.5, 4 replicates each); or pass {"line": ..., "driver": ...} to hold one setting for all 20 batches
control_surface.deliverable_note: model(regime, n, seed) -> DataFrame over exactly ['outcome'], n rows, finite floats. regime.config ALWAYS contains 'line' (an integer 1-5) and 'driver' (0-10, held for all n batches): generate the PROCESS distribution of that line's outcome at that setting. Use ONLY numpy randomness seeded from `seed`. Per-batch spread is real and PRICED (10th and 90th percentiles are graded): do not collapse the distribution to its mean.
